📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-03-eda-consumer-amqp-stopped-publishing`
This is occurrence #3 in the last ~2 weeks (2026-06-20, 2026-07-03, 2026-07-04) — but this one deviates from the first two.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Integrations` (`@connect` / `#team-connect`)
Playbook: Confirm sibling P1 EDA monitors (296632224 event-ingest, 296636101 Kafka-produce) first; if OK, check service:eda_consumer status:error (expect 0); escalate if this occurrence's longer/unresolved shape repeats.
Open Jira: none

Source alerts (1 total, DD-sourced — degraded cycle, no Slack MCP):
  • https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296641466 (last_triggered 2026-07-04T10:21:26Z)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/296641466 (No Data since 10:21:26Z, still open at scan time)
  • DD metric (AMQP consumer, RCA): sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:eda_consumer,env:prod} — data through ~09:49:30Z then zero through 11:10Z (~80min+ gap, still open). Query: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aeda_consumer%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=sum&start=1783157400&end=1783163400
  • Deviation from prior 2 (benign) occurrences: sibling P1 monitors 296632224/296636101 briefly tripped 09:55–10:05:30Z (~10.5min gap) then recovered; upstream ingest/Kafka traffic has been healthy since ~10:05Z while eda_consumer's AMQP-publish metric stayed at zero throughout — decoupled from a simple shared quiet period.
  • eda_consumer status:error logs: 0 hits 09:30–11:10Z (DD Logs query)
  • Full write-up: docs/investigations/2026-07-04-065da57bed22502b.md

:rotating_light: *new alert -- needs human*  (score: 2 mechanical, escalated by judgment override -- see note)
Channel: alert-system  -  bug-type guess: env  -  alerts in group: 1
Owning team (would tag -- not tagged): `CRM Experience`   <- inert text per Hard rule #13

Symptoms:
  - DD monitor 302057011 "[CRM] runtime-core-subscriber throughput dropped (possible stall)" fired for the first time ever (created 2 days ago), 13:07:31Z
  - AMQP command throughput dropped to ~1.17-1.21 msg/s avg, vs a same-cycle-measured baseline of 53.41 msg/s (~46x) -- still depressed as of scan time (13:16:30Z), not yet recovered
  - No corroborating errors: DD logs 0 hits, ES 0 hits, sibling outbound-5xx monitor OK throughout

Trace IDs: n/a (no error traces -- this is a throughput/volume signal, not an exception)
Likely cause: either a genuinely quiet ~26min window (benign, self-recovers) or the Runtime.Core.Subscriber worker has stalled/lost its RabbitMQ connection (runtime-core's own CLAUDE.md documents this exact failure mode: "Cache stale -> Subscriber down -> Start Subscriber.Agent"). Cannot disambiguate from Datadog telemetry alone.
Suggested next action: check RabbitMQ queue depth (Centreon) and the CRM Runtime Workers dashboard per the monitor's own alert text; if queue is genuinely backed up, restart Runtime.Core.Subscriber.Agent. Deploy correlation could not be checked (methodcrm/runtime-core git+gh access both denied this session).

Source alerts (1 total):
  - n/a -- no Slack MCP this session (degraded cycle); DD monitor is the source signal

Evidence:
  - DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302057011 -- "[CRM] runtime-core-subscriber throughput dropped (possible stall)" (Alert)
  - DD sibling monitor (rules out downstream 5xx): https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302056909 (OK)
  - DD metric: https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1783162800&end=1783170990
  - DD logs (0 hits): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%20status%3Aerror%20env%3Aprod&from_ts=1783166400000&to_ts=1783170600000&live=false
  - Kibana: 0 hits in window (not the evidence datasource -- runtime-core-subscriber does not emit to the ES fields.dd_service.keyword index)
  - Full investigation: docs/investigations/2026-07-04-89729b4fe24c5575.md

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #6 for runtime-core-subscriber (1st 13:07:31Z, 2nd 15:10:31Z, 3rd 16:05:31Z, 4th 16:24:31Z — this one) — first-ever notify on this entry, last_notified_at was null.
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `CRM Experience` (`@customer-management` / `#team-customer-management`)
Playbook: Confirm monitor is one of the 5-sibling team:crm AMQP-consumer family; re-run the fired service's own AMQP-rate metric over a multi-hour window — expect a genuine dip below its floor, not a data/tool gap; confirm 0 hits on status:error logs; check sibling monitors for co-firing. Escalate if a fire stays open past ~1h or a sibling error/latency monitor co-fires.
Open Jira: n/a — fix_jira not set

Source alerts (1 total):
  • n/a — degraded cycle (no Slack MCP this session; synthetic hash cf6a1291d838735c = alert_hash(channel=CPHHABKAA, ts=2026-07-04T16:24:31Z))

Evidence:
  • DD monitor: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/302057011 (still `Alert` at scan time — ~45min open, longer than the 5-50min self-recovery seen in occurrences 1-3, no full recovery burst yet)
  • DD metric (evidence_query, RCA): sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:runtime-core-subscriber,env:prod}.as_rate() dipped to a 0.3-2.0 msg/s band from 16:24Z through the end of the queried window (16:59Z), below the 2 msg/s floor. https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.amqp.command.hits&exp_scope=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%2Cenv%3Aprod&exp_agg=avg&start=1783170000&end=1783184400
  • DD logs: https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aruntime-core-subscriber%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1783179000000&to_ts=1783185300000&live=false — 0 hits
  • This-window concentration: sibling monitor method-mobile-notifications-subscriber (302055141) also fired again this same cycle (17:06:21Z, 3rd occurrence, same benign shape) — no new sibling beyond the two already tracked; 3 other siblings (email-subscriber-agent, email-publisher-agent, approutine-subscriber) remain OK since the 2026-07-02 rollout
  • Full write-up: docs/investigations/2026-07-04-cf6a1291d838735c.md (this occurrence) and docs/investigations/2026-07-04-0676543134f4bda1.md (sibling occurrence, suppressed per 24h window)

📒 *known issue recurrence* — `ki-2026-07-04-crm-amqp-consumer-monitor-family-quiet-period-flap`
This is occurrence #10 (combined across sibling monitors) in the last 7 days — every-10th-occurrence resurface (last_notified_at was 2026-07-04T17:12:00Z, still inside the 24h suppression window, but the occurrence-count rule fires anyway).
Owning team (would tag — not tagged): `Admin` (mobile-notifications-stack, per ownership.md:416 — DD monitor tag says `team:crm`, ownership.md disagrees)
Playbook: Confirm shape (monitor is one of the 5 team:crm AMQP-consumer siblings) -> pull sum:trace.amqp.command.hits{service:<name>,env:prod}.as_rate() over a multi-hour window, expect a genuine but brief dip below the monitor's floor -> confirm 0 hits on service:<name> status:error in DD Logs -> check sibling latency/5xx monitor, if also OK this is very likely the benign quiet-period pattern.
Open Jira: none (fix_status: monitoring-noise-suspected-unconfirmed)
